    Fixed #23576 -- Implemented multi-alias fast-path deletion in MySQL backend.
    
    This required moving the entirety of DELETE SQL generation to the

    The MySQL compiler relies on the "DELETE table FROM table JOIN" syntax
    for queries spanning over multiple tables.

result.response:
I have resolved the issue in [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-877__cqo/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1409-L1412) in [compiler.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-877__cqo/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py).

### Cause
When `Model.objects.all().delete()` is executed on a model eligible for fast-delete, `self.query.alias_map` has not yet been populated with the base table alias because no filters or joins have triggered `self.query.get_initial_alias()`. Consequently, [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-877__cqo/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1409-L1412) evaluated to `False` (`0 == 1`), causing [`SQLDeleteCompiler.as_sql()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-877__cqo/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1423-L1440) to fall back to the multi-alias subquery path (`DELETE FROM table WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM table)`).

### Fix
Ensure the base table alias is initialized by calling [`self.query.get_initial_alias()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-877__cqo/django/db/models/sql/query.py#L916-L926) in [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-877__cqo/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1409-L1412) before counting active aliases.
